# `redundant-slice-end`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports a slice operation where the upper bound explicitly specifies
`<slice>.len`.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

In Zig, open-ended slicing syntax `s[start..]` implicitly slices to the end of
the sequence (`s.len`). Explicitly repeating `s[start..s.len]` is redundant and
less idiomatic.

## When it fires

It applies when the upper slice bound is an exact match for the sliced base
expression followed by `.len`.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn tail(bytes: []const u8) []const u8 {
    return bytes[4..bytes.len];
}
```
